previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of mechanical aortic valve replacement, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, coronary artery disease, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for acute onset epigastric tightness and shortness of breath. Evaluation revealed volume overload with pulmonary edema, which resolved after hemodialysis. Cardiac workup showed no evidence of acute myocardial infarction, and symptoms were attributed to acute on chronic decompensated diastolic heart failure. Her INR was subtherapeutic on admission due to recent warfarin hold, and she was managed with heparin and warfarin reinitiation. Testing for pulmonary embolism was deferred given clinical improvement, stable condition, and contrast allergy. She improved clinically, was discharged home with services, and instructed to monitor daily weights and INR with close follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old patient who a poorly healing R BKA stump. 
Patient was admitted on ___ from clinic for debridement of 
her R BKA stump. Her coumadin was held HD#1 due to an INR of 
4.3. On ___, patient was brought to the OR at which time 
all devitalized tissue from her R BKA was debrided and a wound 
VAC was placed. The surgery went well with no apparent 
complications. Her coumadin was restarted following her 
procedure as her INR has reduced to 2.0. Her VAC was changed on 
___ due to a clotting causing the tubing to clog. The patient 
had dialysis preformed on ___ at which time 1.5L was removed. 
Following HD, patient was experiencing some nausea and was given 
zofran which resolved her symptoms. Her VAC was again changed on 
___ and her wound was examined.he wound appeared stable and 
VAC was reapplied.  She was also started on a heparin drip to 
bridge the patient until her INR reached therapeutic levels. Her 
coumadin dosing was increased. On ___ the wound vac was again 
taken down so that the wound bed could be examined. There 
appeared to be good granulation tissue and the vac was 
reapplied. On ___ the patient's INR was still subtherapeutic 
and thus the heparin drip was kept. Additionally the patient was 
weaned off IV pain medications. The skin lesions on the 
patient's fingers continued to be concerning for calciphylaxis. 
Dermatology was consulted, however, they did not feel that the 
lesions were calciphylaxis. On ___ The patient's INR was 2.2. 
The heparin drip was continued. Her vac was changed and her home 
vac was applied. On ___ her INR was 5.1. She was instructed to 
hold her coumadin that night and ___ were set up to check her 
INR in the morning. THis plan was communicated to her PCP. After 
dialysis she was stable and she was discharged. 

Transitional issues: 
1) wound healing: Vac will remain in place with q2-3 day changes 
by ___. She will follow up with Dr. ___ in 3 weeks. 
2) anticoagulation: patient will hold coumadin tonight and will 
be checked in morning of ___ ___s at dialysis on ___. 
Her PCP ___ receive these results and direct her therapy. 
3) Pain control: The patient was requiring elevated doses of 
narcotics in the hospital especially surrounding dressing 
changes.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital after your wound was evaluated 
in clinic and it was determined that you needed surgical 
debridement. You underwent this debridement and vac placement 
and are now ready for discharge. Additionally your 
anticoagulation was supratherapeutic when admitted. This was 
stopped for your surgery and then after your surgery you were 
restarted on your coumadin. You were also placed on a heparin 
drip for clot prophylaxis while your coumadin became 
therapeutic. Please allow us to give you some instructions 
regarding your post operative care. 

1) visiting nurses ___ come and help you as they have been. in 
addition they will assist with the vacuum wound therapy. 
2) please continue your medications and dialysis as you had 
previously. 
3) you have been prescribed some additional pain medication 
above your baseline medications for the surgery, however, you 
should attempt to taper these off back to your baseline 
oxycontin as your pain improves 
4) please follow up with your PCP regarding your coumadin level. 
Your level on the day of discharge was slightly high 5.2. Do not 
take coumadin tonight! The visiting nurses ___ draw the INR 
level from you when you return home. Please coordinate your next 
dose with Dr. ___ who is covering for your PCP this week.
